column1: # KREUZBERG AND REINICKENDORF DEATH INDEXES — ELEVEN VOLUMES, NO HITS, AND TWO NEAR-MISSES OF METHOD.
# Landesarchiv Berlin LABSA. Kreuzberg is P Rep. 510, Reinickendorf is P Rep. 130.
# Both offices hold an unbroken year-by-year run of death name-indexes to 1994. Read 21 September 2026.
# WHY THESE TWO OFFICES. The Schöneberg sweep was for Ella and it found somebody else. These are for
# the other two: AGNES LEIBHOLZ née KERGER at Mehringdamm 109, which is KREUZBERG and not Schöneberg,
# and FRIEDRICH LEIPHOLZ at Schwabstraße 4, which is REINICKENDORF.

# ---------------- THE NEGATIVES, ALL OF THEM BRACKETED ----------------
REINICKENDORF DEATHS 1974 TO 1981
column2: EIGHT CONSECUTIVE YEARS, P Rep. 130 Nr. 1160-1167, and no LEIPHOLZ and no LEIBHOLZ in any of them. The gap the name would sit in, year by year: 1974 Leipelt · LEIPOLT · Leischner — 1975 Leinweber · LEIPZIG — 1976 Leipold · Leipziger — 1977 Leiding · Leistenschneider — 1978 Leidner · Leirer — 1979 LEIPERT · Leisker — 1980 Leinitz · LEIPNER — 1981 Leider · Leischner. EVERY ONE OF THOSE PAIRS STRADDLES WHERE LEIPHOLZ BELONGS, which is what makes these eight negatives and not eight failures to look.

column1: and one near-miss worth naming
column2: the 1974 volume has LEIPOLT and the 1976 volume has LEIPOLD. Neither is Leipholz. They are recorded so that a later reader does not stop at them.

column1: KREUZBERG DEATHS 1980, 1981 AND 1982
column2: P Rep. 510 Nr. 699, 708 and 709. Nothing. 1980 brackets Leipelt · Lenz; 1981 brackets Leimbach · Lenchen; 1982 is read in both its sequences and brackets Leinrich · Lerm in the first and Leieda · Leonore in the second.

column1: WHO WAS BEING LOOKED FOR AND WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE
column2: AGNES is in the Berlin telephone book at Mehringdamm 109 from 1972-73 through 1979-80 and is ABSENT FROM 1980-81, which is why 1980 to 1982 were read first. SHE IS NOT IN THEM. FRIEDRICH is in the books to 1973-74 and absent after, which is why Reinickendorf 1974 onwards was read. HE IS NOT IN THEM EITHER. *** DISAPPEARING FROM A DIRECTORY IS NOT DYING. *** This archive's own control case is Heinrich Leibholz, who vanished from the Berlin directory after 1942 and died in 1948. Both may have moved, entered a home in another borough, or died in a hospital whose district registered the death.

column1: # ---------------- TWO WAYS THE METHOD ALMOST LIED, BOTH CAUGHT ----------------
*** THE BAND WAS TUNED ON THE WRONG VOLUMES AND PRODUCED TWO FALSE NEGATIVES ***
column2: the Schöneberg sweep established that the Le- block sits between 33 and 64 per cent of the way through a volume, and that was carried over to Kreuzberg without checking. KREUZBERG 1980 CAME BACK "no hit" WITH ITS LAST Le- WORD AT LEIPELT, AND 1981 WITH ITS LAST AT LEIMBACH. Both of those sort BEFORE Leipholz. The scan had stopped short of the name and reported an absence it had not looked for. THE FIX IS NOT A WIDER BAND, IT IS AN ASSERTION: a scan now returns the nearest name BEFORE the target and the nearest name AFTER it, and a result with nothing on one side is INCONCLUSIVE and not a negative. Re-run with the assertion, both years genuinely bracket the gap and both negatives stand.

column1: and the assertion immediately earned itself a second time
column2: the first read of Kreuzberg 1982's second sequence came back with an empty "before" list — every name found sorted after Leipholz. Under the old method that would have been published as a negative. The window was moved eighteen pages earlier and the bracket closed properly.

column1: *** AND A BINARY SEARCH THAT DOES NOT WORK ON THESE PAGES ***
column2: the volumes are large and scanning sixty per cent of the pages is slow, so a binary search was tried: take the median word on a page and compare it to the target. IT FAILED COMPLETELY. These registers print a surname column AND a forename column, so the median word on a page is as likely to be Manfred or Karl or Neumann as a surname, and eight probes on Kreuzberg 1982 landed on "sterbe", "hava" and "november". THE ALPHABETICAL KEY OF A PAGE CANNOT BE TAKEN FROM ITS WORDS IN BULK, and this is recorded as a dead end so it is not tried again.

column1: *** AND KREUZBERG 1982 CONTAINS TWO ALPHABETICAL SEQUENCES, NOT ONE ***
column2: 226 pages against about 125 for its neighbours, with L appearing TWICE — "Leuchert" around page 60 and "Leitz" around page 140. A single-sequence assumption would have read half the volume and called the whole year empty. Both sequences were read. ANY VOLUME MUCH LARGER THAN ITS NEIGHBOURS SHOULD BE SUSPECTED OF HOLDING MORE THAN ONE REGISTER.
